At Newland House School we create a happy environment where your child will be encouraged to discover to their own unique passions and interests, and nurtured to achieve their full academic, sporting and creative potential.

Preparing Young Minds For Life
Regardless of the direction the world takes, we understand and anticipate the skills that children will need in the future. We help prepare them to be adaptable, think critically, collaborate effectively and communicate clearly.
Expanding Horizons & Exploring Passions
We will make sure that your child has the freedom to take full advantage of a well-rounded and balanced education that extends far beyond the classroom. We provide a wide-ranging programme of extracurricular activities, where your child will be encouraged to explore their passions or discover new ones, develop their skills, and build confidence.
Cultivating Character & Fostering Empathy
We believe that character is key, and we are committed to helping our pupils to bring out the best in themselves, and those around them. We want to equip them with a moral compass, a strong work ethic, a deep sense of empathy and a desire to make a positive difference to the lives of others and within society.
Embracing Kindness & Building Community
We care passionately about teaching our pupils the core values of kindness, honesty, courage, respect and community. Within our school, we foster an environment where everyone, from pupils to parents and staff, discovers a genuine sense of home.

pageCache.text:
Vision, Aims and Values
Discover our vision for Newland House School and what underpins our ethos
OUR VISION
Our vision is for every child in our School to ‘be their own brilliant’.
Each child will be given incredible opportunities within the classroom and beyond to discover their passions, nurture their talents, become the best version of themselves, be happy and move on to their senior schools with real confidence.
OUR AIMS
We are committed to achieving our vision through the following aims:
To deliver excellence through teaching and innovation to ensure all children realise their full academic potential
To develop well-rounded children through a broad, balanced and engaging curriculum
To provide a richness of opportunity outside the academic curriculum to inspire children’s personal growth and development.
To foster children’s creativity, critical thinking, resilience, and self-awareness to prepare them for success in the 21st century.
To create a positive, inclusive, and supportive school environment that fosters pupils’ success and wellbeing.
To cultivate children’s social and economic understanding and inspire them to be positive and contributing members of society.
we are guided by our core values
Kindness
Be caring, considerate and compassionate to others and towards yourself
Honesty
Bring integrity to all your endeavours
Courage
Always be brave enough to have a go and stand up for your beliefs. Build resilience from failure and confidence from success
Respect
Act and think in a way that acknowledges the feelings and rights of others and the environment
Community
Play your part and get involved to make the School and the wider community better
We are committed to gender neutrality and equal opportunities for everyone.
Diversity is celebrated and everyone in our school community has the opportunity to thrive, regardless of their gender, faith, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, socioeconomic background, or any other characteristic.

Welcome to pre-prep
A very warm welcome to our Pre-Prep, where the Newland House journey begins in the Nursery of our Early Years Hub.
It is in our Pre-Prep that we lay the foundations of a child’s love for learning. We foster a happy, caring environment which ignites curiosity and interest and encourages all of our children to create, experiment, explore and discover their own brilliance.
Choosing a school is a significant decision for parents and we are aware of the trust that you place in us to nurture your little one’s potential. We take great pride in watching our Pre-Prep children flourish and develop as enthusiastic, resilient, and engaged life-long learners, perfectly prepared for their next steps through Newland House and beyond.
“Happiness remains at the core of our Pre-Prep vision; it is the most crucial ingredient to a child’s future success.”
I look forward to speaking to you about all that we have to offer and hope to welcome you into the Newland House community.
Mrs Sophia Excell Deputy Head (Pre-Prep) (Designated Safeguarding Lead)

pageCache.text:
Prep Welcome
Welcome to our Prep School, where we are passionate about inspiring a life-long love of learning and bringing out the brilliance in every child
Our Prep offers a wealth of exciting new experiences and responsibilities that build upon the firm foundations established in Pre-Prep.
Breadth of opportunity remains at the heart of a Newland House education. The creative and sporting areas of school life are as important as any other and children taught by specialist teachers who foster a deep understanding and passion for their subjects. Pupils are challenged in their learning, supported to become increasingly independent and organised, and encouraged to develop critical thinking and effective study skills.
Our excellent pastoral care system ensures that children are happy, secure and well looked after. This supports their academic growth as well as their social, emotional, and physical development.
Your child will join one of four Houses: Saturn, Jupiter, Vulcan or Neptune, and they will represent their House in sporting and music events and compete to earn House points and prizes. The House system instils a strong sense of community and belonging, making all House events calendar highlights!
We empower children to develop their character and take advantage of every opportunity available to them. Roles such as Prefect, House Captain, or Librarian provide real opportunities for responsibility and leadership and Form Captains and Vice Captains represent their classes at the School Council, enabling a diverse range of children to have their voices heard.
We expect all Newland House pupils to be kind and empathetic, always try their best, and contribute positively to both the school and the wider community.
Together, all of this means that children leave us as confident, well-rounded and empathetic individuals who go on to flourish at a range of excellent senior schools.
“Pupils display excellent attitudes to learning and are enthusiastically engaged in all activities.”

About Us
Established in 1897, Newland House is one of the oldest and largest Prep Schools in the area and welcomes children from age 3-13.
A PLACE TO LEARN
The Newland House journey begins in our Nursery at the age of 3 with children also joining us in Reception aged 4. Children progress through the Pre-Prep and will transition to the Prep in Year 3 where they will stay until Year 6 (11+) or Year 8 (13+).
We proudly offer history and tradition alongside modern facilities, progressive teaching methods and a vibrant community.
Our welcoming building sits on a 5-acre site in a quiet residential area on the borders of Twickenham and Teddington. Alongside well-equipped classrooms and ample outdoor space, our pupils benefit from two Science labs, an outstanding Design and Technology workshop, an Art studio and kiln, a Computing suite and a bright and spacious library. We have a purpose-built Music block and two multi-functioning Halls, one of which has retractable seating and a professional lighting and sound system to support the School’s ambitious Drama productions.
Sports Facilities
Onsite Sport facilities include two artificial grass pitches, a hard court and cricket nets. Just a short distance away, we use the extensive grounds of Bushy Park Sports Club for field sports.

pageCache.text:
Drama
The performing arts play an influential role in our School culture. Drama gives all children the opportunity to express their imagination and creativity.
Drama at newland house
Immersing children in the world of theatre not only develops confidence and self-awareness, but also helps to develop strong communication and performance skills.
In Drama, we often explore characters and their journeys, developing empathy skills. We delve into a variety of acting techniques and styles, working from scripts as well as improvising and devising our own pieces. We pride ourselves in the quality of our performances and every child has many opportunities to shine on stage, enabling them to hone their skills and create memories.
Our Prep Hall has retractable seating and a professional light and sound system to support our ambitious productions. Pupils also have the chance to explore technical theatre, and are given the opportunity to assist with lighting, sound and other technical elements during productions.
LAMDA Lessons
Each week , over 100 pupils participate in LAMDA lessons. If your child has a real passion for acting or would like to work on valuable communication and presentation skills, we offer sessions at School with one of our highly trained visiting LAMDA teachers

pageCache.text:
Music
Our vibrant Music department is housed in a recently updated Music block, complete with modern practice spaces and professional-level equipment.
Music at Newland House
Learning music with a specialist teacher, all our pupils are encouraged to experience the joy of performing and creating music.
Outside of timetabled lessons, there are many opportunities for children to play a musical instrument or join an ensemble or choir. Approximately 70% of our pupils take advantage of the wealth of experience that our visiting peripatetic music teachers offer through one-to-one lessons from Year 1 upwards. Lessons are offered across a broad spectrum of orchestral instruments, singing, drums and guitar. Pupils can enter for graded music examinations which are held each term.
Young musicians can join a variety of choirs and ensembles, some of which are open to all abilities and others by invitation to pupils with particular musical talent and aspiration.
Our choirs include: Year 1 and 2, Year 3 and 4, Year 4 Voices, Newland House Choir, Senior Boys’ Choir and a Chamber Choir. Recent tours have included Belgium, Cornwall and other parts of the UK.
Ensembles include: Orchestra, Training Orchestra, Jazz Band, Guitar, Recorder, Ukulele, Pop-Rock Bands, Strings, Wind, African Drums, plus songwriting and theory groups.
There are many performance opportunities for all pupils, from informal concerts which are great fun and well attended to larger events such as the Summer Concert held at the Landmark Arts Centre, Teddington, a Choral Day at Wellington College and the Richmond Music Festival.
Additional support is offered to pupils preparing for Music Scholarships and over the years many of our pupils have been successful in gaining Scholarships to senior schools.

pageCache.pageTitle: Community Partnerships and Charitable Support | Newland House School
pageCache.text:
Community Partnerships and Charitable Support
Newland House plays an active role within the community, investing in shared community sports facilities, supporting local and national charities, and offering the use of our facilities.
Bushy Park Sports Club (BPSC)
Newland House enjoys an on-going partnership with Bushy Park Sports Club (formerly the National Physical Laboratory Sports Club), ideally located on the borders of Bushy Park.
Our pupils benefit from their excellent and well-maintained facilities for field sports practice and fixtures, and we’re proud to have invested considerably in the redevelopment of the clubhouse to the mutual benefit of the local community.
Bushy Park Sports Club is managed by a group of volunteer trustees who are dedicated to offering sports, fitness and social activities to as many local people as possible. These include football, hockey, tennis, cricket, table tennis, dance, yoga and pilates as well as the use of the gym.
Charitable Fundraising
Throughout the year we are involved in raising money for a variety of charities. From an early age, we encourage children to help others, recognise those less fortunate than themselves and learn to become caring world citizens.
Each year, our Head Boy and Head Girl select a charity and many of our fundraising activities throughout the year, such as quizzes, sponsored events and sales are in support of their named charity.
Charities supported over the year have included Great Ormond Street Hospital and Children’s Charity; Street Invest; React, (Rapid Effective Assistance for Children with potentially Terminal illness; Momentum – who support families and children being treated for cancer in the local Boroughs; Horse Rangers Association – who support Riding for the Disabled and Keen London who operate free weekly sports and recreation sessions for children and young adults with learning, behavioural and physical disabilities. We also regularly support other charities including MacMillan Cancer Support, Ruils, the Anti-Bullying Alliance and Children in Need.
Use of our facilities
We are delighted to share our facilities with local organisations and community groups.
Otakar Kraus Music Trust
The Otakar Kraus Music Trust (OKMT) regularly hold weekend music workshops in our music department. The Trust provides music therapy and music projects for over 450 people of all ages with physical, learning, neurological or psychological difficulties in order to improve their wellbeing and quality of life.
Teddingtones Community Choir
The Teddingtones Community Choir rehearses every Wednesday evening from 8.15pm to 9.45pm in the Pre-Prep Hall.
Led by Teddington local and professional singer and vocal coach, Laura Luck, the choir welcomes singers of all abilities who want to experience the joy of singing and meeting new people!
They are a friendly group who enjoy performing everything from classical to musical theatre to pop. It’s a relaxed and fun atmosphere (with a little chocolate and wine thrown in for good measure!), so whether you’re an experienced chorister who can read music or a complete novice who simply loves singing, they’d love you to get involved.
Jo Yoga
Regular yoga classes take place at in our Pre-Prep Hall. Run by Jo, a Yoga Alliance registered teacher who has practised yoga for 30 years in the UK, California and Costa Rica.
Wednesday, 6:30pm – 7:30pm
Saturday, 8:30am – 9:30am
£12 drop in. For local residents, the first class is free.

Governors
The Governors of the school serve as Directors and Trustees of Newland House School Trust Limited, which is both a company limited by guarantee and also a registered charity.
Newland House School Trust Limited owns the school and there are no external shareholders or investors.
The Governors’ main objective is to maintain the stability and success of a co-educational family school by investing for the future and for the benefit of pupils. The key element of the Trust’s present strategy revolves around the continuing review of the School’s facilities to ensure that they meet the needs of current and future pupils.
Mrs Bean Hobday Chair of Governors & Safeguarding Committee
Bean graduated from Cambridge University in Natural Sciences. After graduation she joined Mars where she moved through the Graduate Trainee Scheme and a number of management roles within the Petfood, Confectionery and Drinks businesses. She has been the National Graduate Marketing Manager and her last role was Global Marketing Director at Mars Drinks. After a fantastic 12 year career with Mars she chose to leave to start a family. Bean is married to Dave and lives in Teddington, and their three children all attended Newland House School. She had an active role within the school community during her time as a parent and is delighted to remain connected to the School through the governor role and her place on the school’s Safeguarding Committee.
Mr Matthew Alexander Finance and General Purposes Committee
Matt is a corporate finance and business consultant with a passion for education and an interest in the Independent sector. Matt was educated at St Paul’s Juniors and Eton College, and read English at Christ Church, Oxford. Following ten years at Smith Square Partners LLP, financial and strategic advisors to private, public and government organisations, including the education sector, Matt became the CEO of the Anglo-Chinese School of London from 2021-2024. ACSL owns Kensington Wade, an innovative English-Chinese bilingual prep school in West London, where Mr Skelton is member of the school’s advisory board. Matt lives in Shepherds Bush and has a daughter in the early stages of her prep school education.
Mr Harry Mann Finance and General Purposes Committee
Harry was educated at the Royal Grammar School High Wycombe and at Cambridge University where he studied Natural Sciences. After graduation he joined Shell where he qualified as an accountant and as an MBA while working in Finance in Aberdeen, London, North West England, Oman and Thailand. After leaving Shell, Harry worked for another oil and gas company, a mining company and a workplace consultancy. Harry is married to Clare, they live in Teddington, and their two daughters and son all attended Newland House.
Mr Jon Peachey Estates Committee
Jon was educated at St.George’s College in Weybridge, Surrey. He has a BSc in Geology from the City of London Polytechnic (1987) and an MSc and DIC in Applied Geology from Imperial College, London (1988). Thereafter, embarking on a 30 year career in the Energy Industry for major and mid-size operating companies in technical, commercial financial and management roles. Jon sits on advisory boards in various roles at Imperial College and the University of Utah.
Jon and the family have completed assignments in Brazil, Canada and several UK locations. Jon is married with two boys, who both attended Newland House. He lives in Teddington and plays hockey and cricket locally.
Mrs Bayan Carter Finance and General Purposes Committee
Bayan was born and grew up in Kazakhstan. When the Soviet Union collapsed, she won a scholarship for a one-year study at an American high school. She completed her bachelor’s degree in International Finance at the Kazakh State University of Management and came to the UK to pursue an MBA at an American International University in Richmond. Bayan is an Associate Director at the Private Equity department at the EBRD, an international institution that operates in emerging markets. She has worked on over 100 investments, mostly banks in over 20 countries. She is currently a member of the Board of Directors at a start-up challenger bank – TBC Uzbekistan. Bayan lives in Twickenham with her husband and two children, one of them has attended Newland House.
Miss Polly Holmes Safeguarding Governor
Polly graduated from Exeter University with a degree in Biological Sciences before working for NatWest Bank for a few years. After seeing the error of her ways, she completed a PGCE and has been happily teaching Biology A level and Chemistry GCSE ever since. She has been teaching at Hampton School for over 18 years, having previously taught at schools in Berkshire and Sussex. Her current role as Assistant Head involves various aspects of pupil wellbeing, safeguarding, pastoral care, PSHE strategy and behaviour management. She is a big supporter of the Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme and regularly assesses and supervises expeditions when she can. She has accompanied senior school pupils on a variety of month-long expeditions to far-flung destinations, and on Saturday mornings she tries to be out on the river paddling a dragon boat.
Ms Nasreen Janmohamed Human Resources Committee
Nasreen is a senior HR professional having worked in several industries across her career to date. Having graduated from the University of Nottingham and gained post graduate qualifications from Manchester and Leeds Business Schools, she is currently in a senior HR position in a Hospital where her role spans across employee relations, employee wellbeing, diversity and inclusion, recruitment and change management. A particular passion of hers is equity, diversity and inclusion and this is one of the reasons that she wanted to become a governor at the school and has a deep interest in pedagogy and how this influences educational outcomes. Other interests include running, reading and theatre.
Mrs Madeline Walsh Finance and General Purposes Committee
Madeline studied Politics at the University of Sussex before joining PricewaterhouseCoopers, where she qualified as both a Chartered Tax Advisor and a Chartered Accountant. She began her career specialising in Expatriate Tax, before moving into Corporate Tax and later International Tax and M&A. Madeline joined Bupa in 2011, initially focusing on tax matters relating to acquisitions before progressing into a senior role evaluating the company’s international acquisition targets.
Madeline now holds several pro bono roles. In her free time, she enjoys cycling and competing in triathlons, representing Team GB in her age group. Madeline lives in Esher with her husband, Ken, and their two children, both of whom attended Newland House School from Nursery onwards.

Parents’ Association
Our active Parents’ Association (PA) brings the wider school community together through social events and fundraising.
The PA is run by a Board of Trustees who are voted in annually at the AGM, and who create an event and fund-raising calendar. They hold 5 or 6 events a year including a Fireworks night, and the Christmas and Summer Fairs.
Alongside promoting a sense of community, these events also raise money for school projects and chosen charities. In recent years, we have supported Skylarks, Ruils and the Hunger Project charities, and funded items such as new playground equipment for the Pre-Prep, author visits, and a young enterprise programme for older pupils in the school.
JOINING THE PA
Parents at Newland House are friendly and welcoming, and the PA encourages the whole school community to help with events. Taking on one of the organising roles will mean you are part of the event team and part of creating a vibrant school community. It is a fantastic way to get involved and have fun with other parents. If everyone takes on a role it shares the load, and gives us all a chance to get to know other parents and carers across the school. Getting involved through the PA also gives parents who might not have the chance to meet others at the school gate, the opportunity to make new friends and contribute to the school
Where can I hear more?
Sign up to the Parents’ Association X account @NewlandHousePA for updates on events, how charities and the school are benefiting from monies raised, and to give you up to date information on any new PA initiatives.
Becoming a Class Representative
Three volunteer Class Representatives are chosen from each class and usually serve for the whole school year. In Reception, they are often parents of older children in the school who know the ropes! After that, anyone is welcome to volunteer. Class Reps attend termly meetings with the PA and with the Senior Leadership Team, organise termly social events for their class including informal coffee mornings and evening drinks for parents and carers, and also help co-ordinate volunteers from their year group for school events.
“I really enjoyed being a Class Rep, it was lovely helping to promote the community aspect of school life to parents. It was a fulfilling role, as many of the events we promoted raised money for the school and for meaningful charities. It was also interesting being involved in meetings with the PA and SLT and hearing first-hand about the school vision.”

Visits and Visitors
The Pre-Prep experience is enriched by the range of visitors who come in to see us and the variety of trips we are able to take.
Visits
Capitalising on our proximity to London and sometimes heading a little further afield, day trips to places such as the Wetland Centre and Painshill Park weave real-life experiences into our pupils’ education and enrich their learning.
Always a favourite with our children is the annual Nursery trip out to Bocketts Farm where we get to take a coach and spend a whole day learning and discovering!
Visitors
We regularly invite guests in to deliver workshops which ignite curiosity and foster hands-on learning, such as indulging in a chocolate workshop or meeting a real explorer.
We enjoy workshops with local theatre companies, as well as regular visits from the older pupils from the Prep school. Each year, a number of different animals come and see us too, such as reindeer at Christmas, living eggs and caterpillars!

Art
We foster creativity in our Art room, allowing children to experience the pride and satisfaction of bringing their unique visions to life.
Art at Newland House
During weekly Art lessons, pupils delve into the works of successful artists, craftspeople, and designers, and hone their skills across a diverse range of media, including drawing, painting, textiles, and ceramics.
Our meticulously planned, skills-based Art curriculum ensures a progressive development of artistic abilities. You child will learn to use line to describe form and apply tone to achieve 3D effects. They will draw from observation, using various media such as charcoal, graphite sticks, and pastels. In painting, children master the art of mixing secondary and tertiary colours and employ acrylic, watercolour, and gouache, inspired by contemporary artists’ works.
Our curriculum also encompasses modelling techniques using clay, plasticine, and other materials, with finished pieces glazed and fired in our own kiln. Additionally, students work with wire and textiles, broadening their artistic repertoire.
Guided by our specialist Art teacher, the works produced by our pupils consistently reflect an exceptionally high standard. Our students regularly participate in local and national art competitions and exhibitions, showcasing their talents.
The Art room buzzes with activity even during break times, hosting various clubs and Art Scholarship support groups that provide further opportunities for creative expression.

Design Technology
In our impressive Design and Technology department your child will gain confidence in making their ideas a reality using various materials including wood, metal, plastics and electronic components.
Design Technology at Newland House
Pupils are shown the importance of the design process from their initial design concept idea through to development, modelling and a finished product.
With careful support and guidance, they learn to use a comprehensive range of handheld and machine tools in a workshop where they can explore traditional and modern manufacturing techniques.
Our pupils have access to a range of modern CAD/CAM equipment including a 3D printer, 3D scanner, vinyl cutter and laser cutter all of which are controlled by software such as 2D Design, Autodesk Fusion, and Trimble SketchUp. Robotics, programming, and problem solving are taught as part of the curriculum and in STEM Club through VEQ Robotics and Sphero Education

Learning Enrichment
support And Extension
Newland House is an inclusive School, and our Learning Enrichment Department works together with parents and families to ensure that every child here makes the best possible progress, meets their targets, and discovers their own brilliance.
We celebrate and support neurodiversity and recognise everyone experiences the world differently.
There may be times when a class teacher feels a child would benefit from an intervention group to support their learning and help them achieve their best. These groups might also help a child catch up in a particular skill area.
We offer a range of enrichment groups as part of our everyday provision, including Social and Emotional, Phonics, Fine Motor, Social and Communication, Jump Ahead, and Maths and English. Newland House is also a member of NACE (National Association for Able Children in Education) and MENSA, allowing us to cater for the more able learners and offer suitable levels of challenge and stretch. Sometimes, the class teacher may suggest one-to-one sessions in numeracy or literacy with one of our experienced specialist teachers, who are all trained at SpLD Level 5 or above. These sessions support children with specific learning difficulties, including Dyslexia, Dyscalculia, Autistic Spectrum Disorder, ADHD, and Developmental Language Disorder.
With a deep understanding of neurodiversity, our weekly targeted tuition identifies gaps in knowledge and provides strategies that pupils can implement. This small-step, achievable, memorable, and multisensory approach helps children feel supported and confident as they grow in self-esteem and ensures greater access to the curriculum. (This is offered at an additional cost.)
Further Information
If you are considering joining us from another educational setting and have a child with special educational needs or disabilities, please contact us in advance of registering to make sure that we can offer them the support they need from the moment they arrive.
Contact our admissions team on 0208 865 1305 or email us at admissions@newlandhouse.net

pageCache.text:
Learning Enrichment
Newland House is an inclusive school, and we are passionate about ensuring that every child here makes the best possible progress, meets their targets and discovers their own brilliant.
The Learning Enrichment Department is an integral part of our school and works closely together with children and their parents.
As all children progress at different rates, there may be times when a class teacher feels a child would benefit from an intervention group to support their learning and help them overcome any challenges they made be experiencing or catch up in a particular skill.
We celebrate neurodiversity and recognise that everyone experiences the world differently. Sometimes, the class teacher may suggest one-to-one sessions in Numeracy or Literacy with one of our experienced specialist teachers, who are all trained at SpLD Level 5 or above. These sessions support children with specific learning difficulties, including Dyslexia, Dyscalculia, Autistic Spectrum Disorder, ADHD, and Developmental Language Disorder. We do not see different as a deficit and believe there are no ‘normal’ ways of thinking or learning.
With a deep understanding of neurodiversity, our weekly targeted tuition identifies gaps in knowledge and provides strategies that pupils can implement. This small-step, achievable, memorable, and multisensory approach helps children feel supported and confident as they grow in self-esteem and ensures greater access to the curriculum. (This is offered at an additional cost.)
More able pupils
Through our policy of teaching to the top, we emphasise high expectations and high-quality, challenging teaching for all. This provision is further enriched and extended by targeted interventions and activities for our more able pupils.
The More Able programme aims to stimulate, challenge, and support pupils in their individual passions and talents. We offer both internal and external opportunities to enhance learning experiences. These include History trips focused on World War II, public speaking courses, talks from STEM specialists, and creative writing competitions.
As a member of NACE (National Association for Able Children in Education) and recognised as a MENSA school, we are committed to excellence in education and offering suitable levels of challenge and stretch.
English as an additional Language (EAL)AIMS
Our EAL specialist evaluates children for whom English is a second language and offers tailored weekly sessions based on individual needs.
These sessions are typically conducted in pairs or very small groups, focusing on areas such as vocabulary building, verbal role-play, and reading comprehension to ensure each child’s linguistic and academic progress.

Sport
Sport and Physical Education play an important role in Newland House School life and we are proud of our sporting reputation.
Sport for all
Our ethos is ‘Sport for all’ where each child gets the opportunity to develop their potential to the best of their ability.
We are dedicated to nurturing skills, boosting confidence and growing competence. And it is not just about sports – children learn essential life skills like teamwork, discipline, handling wins and losses, and embracing a healthy lifestyle.
We introduce the core sports of Football, Netball, Hockey, Rugby and Cricket through our Games curriculum. It is important to us that both girls and boys have equal opportunities to participate in all sports offered.
Sports per Term
AUTUMN TERM
Spring Term
Summer Term
A spirit of Healthy competition
Our commitment to inclusivity goes hand in hand with fostering a spirit of healthy competition.
All children will get a chance to represent the School in regular competitive interschool fixtures, local and national tournaments or House competitions. Swimming, which the children enjoy from Year 3 upwards, is fully inclusive and offers opportunities for children to develop confidence and ability in the water as well as take part in regular galas.
Our Physical Education lessons focus on acquiring skills, understanding the demands and benefits of physical activity, and having fun in an engaging environment. Children are introduced to a broader range of sports and activities such as Gymnastics, Tennis, Badminton and Basketball.

pageCache.pageTitle: Extra Curricular Clubs, Music Tuition and LAMDA | Newland House School
pageCache.text:
Extra Curricular Clubs, Music Tuition and LAMDA
Extra-curricular Clubs
At Newland House, you can choose from over 70 different clubs which means that there is something to inspire and excite everyone.
We’re passionate about participation and will encourage your child to explore their interests and talents outside of the school timetable.
Clubs run before school, during lunchtime and afterschool. Many are led by our own teachers and are free to attend, those run by external providers will be billed termly.
Individual Music Lessons
Outside of lessons, there is an array of opportunities to play a musical instrument and around 70% of children learn a musical instrument at school.
Our highly skilled peripatetic music teachers offer individual lessons from Year 1 in a huge range of instruments, such as violin, viola, cello, double bass, flute, oboe, clarinet, saxophone, bassoon, trumpet, trombone, French horn, piano, guitar and drums. Children can learn classical singing and there’s also pop singing and song writing, music theory and acting and music technology available.
Individual lessons will be on a rotating timetable so the children will come out of their lessons at a different time each week.
Small group Lessons
In Years 1 and 2, children also have the option to learn violin, cello and recorder in small groups.
Arrangements for lessons and payment are organised directly with the visiting music teacher.
Lamda
LAMDA (London Academy of Dramatic Art ) is a world leading drama school and examinations provider.
Our experienced visiting LAMDA teacher offers 30-minute weekly lessons in communication and performance. Lessons help empower children to become confident communicators and are given during school hours on a rotating timetable. By this system, your child will rarely miss the same subject more than two or three times a term. They will be encouraged to take LAMDA examinations when the teacher feels they are ready – exams can be taken externally or at school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wrap Around Care and Holiday Club | Newland House School
pageCache.text:
Wrap Around Care and Holiday Club
School hours can be challenging for busy and working parents. Our Wrap Around Care gives you the option to extend the school day and covers 17 weeks of the year.
MORNING WRAP AROUND HOLIDAY CARE
Wrap Around Care is available for all children from Nursery upwards and children are supervised by a team of qualified and experienced staff.
The morning session starts at 7:30am in the Prep Dining Hall and includes a daily choice of a freshly cooked breakfast, toast, cereal, croissants, fruit, milk and juice. It’s a relaxed and enjoyable start to the day with activities available such as board games, drawing, construction, imaginative and outdoor play.
At 8:20am, children will be taken to their classrooms for the start of school (or older children will make their own way to their form room).
AFTERNOON WRAP AROUND
Afternoon wrap around care starts when school or clubs end until 5pm or 6pm. Children will be offered an after-school snack of sandwiches and fruit.
We create an environment where children can wind down at the end of the day. They can participate in activities such as arts and crafts, board games, construction and outdoor play, as well as having a quiet area where they can complete homework.
For children in Pre-Prep or Nursery the sessions will take place in the Pre-Prep building, and for children in the Prep school, sessions take place in the Prep Dining Hall.
SIBLING CLUB
The Nursery and Pre-Prep day runs until 3:20pm so we offer a free sibling club until 3:45pm to help parents who want to coordinate pick-up with another child in the Prep School which finishes at 3:50pm.
Holiday Club – 17 weeks of the year
As fun as school holidays are, they can be a real juggle for parents!
Open to children in Nursery to Year 8, our in-house Holiday Club will cover 17 weeks of the school holidays – all of the school holidays aside from the Christmas/New year period. The club is multi-activity based, run in familiar surroundings with familiar members of staff and amongst friends. Special ‘themed’ weeks include Drama and Sport.
The club runs from 9am until 4pm each day or 8:30am until 5:30pm for those needing extended hours.
